import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import os

# Load data
# Security: Check file existence before reading to prevent FileNotFoundError DoS
if os.path.exists("data/stablecoin_marketcap.csv"):
    df = pd.read_csv("data/stablecoin_marketcap.csv")

    # Ensure date is datetime
    # Security: Date parsing uses errors="coerce" to prevent Denial of Service (DoS) from unhandled DateParseError/ValueError if the CSV contains malformed data.
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"], errors="coerce")

    # Security: Enforce explicit numeric conversion for market_cap to prevent unhandled exceptions (DoS) when plotting
    df["market_cap"] = pd.to_numeric(df["market_cap"], errors="coerce")

    df = df.dropna(subset=["date", "market_cap"])

    # Security: Check for empty dataframe before plotting to prevent ValueError with NaT
    if not df.empty:
        # Line Plot
        fig = px.line(df, x="date", y="market_cap", color="coin_name", title="Stablecoin Market Cap Over Time")
        fig.show()
    else:
        print("No valid data available for Market Cap History.")
else:
    # Initialize empty df to avoid undefined variable in next block
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["date", "market_cap", "coin_name"])
    print("Market Cap data file not found.")
# Security: Check for empty dataframe before applying operations that fail on NaT (e.g. strftime)
if not df.empty:
    # Get latest date
    latest_date = df['date'].max()
    latest_df = df[df['date'] == latest_date].copy()

    # Sort by market cap descending
    latest_df = latest_df.sort_values(by='market_cap', ascending=False)

    # Pie Chart
    fig_pie = px.pie(latest_df, values='market_cap', names='coin_name', title=f'Market Dominance ({latest_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")})')
    fig_pie.show()
else:
    print("No valid data available for Market Dominance.")
